result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the function returns `refreshTokenResponse` (the zod safeParse wrapper object), not `.data`. In GoogleCalendarService the old code did `const key = googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` and stored it; the new code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and stores `{ key }` via prisma, so the stored credential becomes `{success, data, error}` wrapper instead of the parsed keys — corrupting credentials after refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`) rather than the parsed payload (`.data`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is assigned to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store the wrapper object instead of the credential key shape, corrupting stored Google Calendar credentials after refresh. (Other call sites like Office365 treat the return value as a wrapper, but Google does not.)
